steps.code:
# Let's parse all note contents to extract date and habit values
import re

# Define the habit order from the first note (468)
first_note = note_contents[0]  # note 468
content_lines = first_note['content'].split('\n')
habits = []
for line in content_lines:
    if ':' in line and not line.startswith('#'):
        habit_name = line.split(':')[0].strip()
        habits.append(habit_name)
print("Habit order:", habits)

# Now parse all notes
parsed_rows = []
for note_data in note_contents:
    # Extract date from title: "Habit Tracking Log for 2023-05-17"
    match = re.search(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', note_data['title'])
    if not match:
        print(f"Warning: no date found in title: {note_data['title']}")
        continue
    date_str = match.group(1)
    
    # Parse content to get habit values
    content = note_data['content']
    values = {}
    for line in content.split('\n'):
        if ':' in line and not line.startswith('#'):
            parts = line.split(':', 1)
            habit = parts[0].strip()
            val = parts[1].strip().lower()
            values[habit] = val
    
    # Build row in the order of habits
    row = {'date': date_str}
    for h in habits:
        row[h] = values.get(h, 'no')  # default to 'no' if missing
    parsed_rows.append(row)

print(f"Parsed {len(parsed_rows)} rows")
print("Sample row:", parsed_rows[0])
